description: ecoinvent 3.13 publishes a new LCIA implementation workbook. Since #454 the list was merged with its factors fetched and unread, because the method file named one ecoinvent Centre implementation, read from 3.12. This reads the 3.13 workbook as a second implementation of the same publisher, `ecoinvent Centre (3.13)` on the slug `ecoinvent-centre-3-13`, beside the 3.12 one, `ecoinvent Centre (3.12)` on the slug `ecoinvent-centre` that release 1.1.0 published its category identifiers under. The slug `ecoinvent-centre` is the 3.12 workbook for good, and every later workbook carries its release in slug and name. Both workbooks decide: two releases are two statements, and a number that moved between them is a question rather than the newer release winning by default. They are one publisher, so where only the two of them state a number and agree, that is a proposal and not `agreed`. The 3.13 workbook is closed: ecoinvent publishes no 3.13 file in its public LCIA repository, so its numbers inform this list's and none is written to the database or either factor file under its name. What it changes, on the build named in the pull request: the lindane and endosulfan isomers, which the 3.12 workbook scores with the parent's numbers and the 3.13 workbook with their own, become questions between the two releases rather than being settled by either.

expectations.title: The 3.12 workbook's factors are published under `ecoinvent Centre (3.12)`
expectations.comment: 27,346 on the build of `1e67f3c`, over 7,939 flows; `at_least`, because a merge that reaches a few more or fewer of 3.12's rows should not fail the claim that the implementation is there. That the 3.13 workbook is read in full is `0766-every-factor-ecoinvent-states-is-read`.

expectations.title: The 3.13 workbook's factors are matched onto this list's flows and none is published
expectations.comment: The count `characterise` writes for a closed implementation in place of `factors_published`: what reached a flow and was handed to the consensus derivation, and was written nowhere. 27,342 on the build of `1e67f3c`.

expectations.title: EF 3.1's 25 categories are published under its four open implementations and not under the closed one
expectations.comment: 100 for EF 3.1 -- the JRC, the 3.12 workbook, GreenDelta and this list -- and Stepwise 2006's 38. The 3.13 workbook's 25 are minted for the run, because its factors are keyed on them, and never written: a category row nobody can see the factors of would say an implementation exists that does not. An equality, so that opening it is a change somebody makes on purpose.

expectations.title: A kilogram of alpha-endosulfan to unspecified air is worth the JRC's 42,351 for freshwater ecotoxicity
expectations.comment: The JRC and the 3.13 workbook state the isomer's own 42,351; the 3.12 workbook scored the alpha rows with the parent's 11,499 (#456). The ecoinvent Centre is one publisher whichever release speaks, so this is the JRC against one of the Centre's releases, a contested question, and until the ruling in `lcia-factor-rulings.json` this list published nothing here. The ruling publishes the JRC's number for all 84 contested factors of the five isomers, where the 3.12 workbook states the parent's number in every one.

expectations.title: The 3.12 workbook's 11,499 for the same flow is published under its own name
expectations.comment: The other side of the question above, published under the 3.12 workbook's own name.

expectations.title: Nothing is published for the same flow under the 3.13 workbook's name
expectations.comment: It states 42,351 here, and that number is one of the three the question above is between; the workbook is closed, so it is read and not republished.

expectations.title: The proposed-factor queue holds no more open items than it did on the build this change was measured on
expectations.comment: A ceiling, as `0752-the-proposed-queue-shrank` is. 32 open items on main's build of `8593061`, with the 3.12 workbook deciding alone; 50 on the build of `1e67f3c` (run `20261123T2334105411510000`) with both deciding. The 18 added: eight for `Sodium Stearyl Fumarate` and `Monostearyl Fumarate`, the two rows 3.13 is the first list to ship, which only it scores; and ten for the α- and β-hexachlorocyclohexane rows only ecoinvent characterises, where 3.12 states lindane's number and 3.13 the isomer's own. The rulings on the lindane and endosulfan isomers answer eighteen proposed items, those ten among them, which leaves 32.

expectations.title: A kilogram of α-endosulfan to silvicultural soil is worth 3.13's 28,211 for freshwater ecotoxicity
expectations.comment: Silvicultural soil is a compartment only ecoinvent has, so the JRC is silent and the two releases are the evidence: 3.12 states endosulfan's 4,420.3 and 3.13 the isomer's own 28,211. One number from the closed 3.13 workbook published for one flow, which the closed flag allows; the workbook as a whole is still withheld. Stands for the 14 silvicultural questions of the five isomers.
